decisions.title: Key, mode and chord are inferred by ONE joint decode
decisions.verbatim:
Key, mode, and chord are inferred by ONE probabilistic decode
> over `(tonic, mode, chord)` with segmentation as a modeled (semi-Markov) variable and every enumerated clue
> as a theory-grounded factor
decisions.plain: The tonality, the major/minor character and the chord are not worked out one after another. They are worked out together, in a single pass that also decides where one chord ends and the next begins.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:3 (GOVERNING DECISION banner); OPEN_ITEMS.md:15-26
decisions.rationale: Theory basis cited at ARCHITECTURE.md:9 - `cowork_key_chord_joint_inference_grounding.md`; the forcing constraint is the circular dependency list at ARCHITECTURE.md:637-651 (key<->chord, segmentation<->chord, non-chord-tone<->chord, function<->chord identity), which a feed-forward pipeline cannot resolve correctly.

compiles the five committed artifacts + the selected weight vector

decisions.plain: The numbers the estimator was trained on are built into the program at compile time rather than read from disk at run time, so a running copy cannot quietly disagree with the numbers we published.

decisions.verbatim:
State = `24 keys × a ground-truth-derived Roman-numeral
> vocabulary`, chord = scale-degree-valued (the chord symbol is the derived published fact from (key, degree)), segmentation is a modeled semi-Markov variable, seg_cap 4.
decisions.plain: The estimator chooses among 24 tonalities and a list of chord roles read off the annotated corpus; a chord is named by its role in the key, and the chord symbol is worked out from that. One chord may span at most four consecutive events.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:43-44 cites cowork_joint_estimator_factorization.md as the full specification. decisions.title: The published scores are log-scores, not probabilities
decisions.verbatim:
The scores are LOG-scores, NOT probabilities, and gaps
> are score differences
decisions.plain: The numbers beside each alternative are not chances of being right. They are model scores, and the difference between two of them is a score gap, not a percentage.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:54-56; the true-probability step is deferred to OI-193

decisions.verbatim:
WHOLE-score decode ONCE; deterministic; NO caching (a

decisions.title: Failure is unambiguous - never a partial record, never a silent fallback
decisions.verbatim: never a partial record, never a silent fallback (#13).
decisions.plain: If the analysis cannot be produced, the program says so and returns nothing. It never returns half an answer or quietly falls back to the old method.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:116-117; restated at :205-206 for the note seam
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:117 - #13, a surprise is surfaced as a stop rather than built around: a partial record or a silent fallback would hide the failure from the caller.

decisions.title: Which staves feed the analysis is decided at the fact adapter, not by a later filter
decisions.verbatim:
INPUT selection at the fact
> adapter (the layer that owns its input surface, #7), before the note enters the L1 fact view the decode reads; NOT a
> consumer-side post-filter, NOT an inference change
decisions.plain: When a staff is excluded from analysis - for instance the chord staff the program itself writes to - its notes are dropped before the analysis starts, not filtered out of the answer afterwards.
decisions.status_source: open_items/OI-204 (RESOLVED 2026-07-27); confirmed at jointnotationproducer.h:72-73
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:119-123: input selection belongs at the layer that owns its input surface (#7), and doing it there is what stops a populated chord staff's own notes from being fed back into a re-analysis - the self-feedback hazard the legacy design guarded against (ARCHITECTURE.md:5437-5438).

decisions.title: The two seams read the record as pure views - no recomputation
decisions.verbatim: The two §1 seams READ this record as pure VIEWS (#6, no recompute)
decisions.plain: The two ways of asking the record a question - 'what is in this stretch of music' and 'what is at this moment' - only look things up. Neither works anything out for itself.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:125-131; confirmed at jointnotationproducer.h:86-90
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:125 - #6, one path per concern: a view cannot disagree with the record it reads, a second computation can.

a boundary

decisions.verbatim:
**THE BOUNDARY
> IS PERMANENTLY GUARDED both ways** by a mechanical include-closure test

decisions.title: The key-exposure bucket is decided once, at one site
decisions.verbatim: The implode reads the stored bucket (#6 — one thresholding site per gate).
decisions.plain: How confident the program is about the tonality is turned into 'below tentative / tentative / assertive' in exactly one place, and everything downstream reads that answer instead of deciding again.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:165-171; open_items/OI-182 (EXECUTED at the record surface)
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:171 - #6, one thresholding site per gate: the bucket is set once at the section-layer set site and the implode reads it, instead of each consumer re-thresholding.

`keyConfidence` = the RAW §3.3
> key-axis gap in nats (a model-internal quantity, NO [0,1] remap)
decisions.plain: The confidence value carried on the record arm is the estimator's own raw score gap, on its own scale - deliberately not converted into a 0-to-1 number.

decisions.verbatim:
The bounded-window decode
> cache is BYPASSED on the record arm (a whole-score produce per invocation, the P3a/P4 pattern; a record cache is a later
> measured concern
decisions.plain: Clicking a note re-analyses the whole score. The old shortcut that reused a small window's work is not used on the new path, and no replacement has been built yet.
decisions.status_source: open_items/OI-203 (OPEN, priority raised post-switch); open_items/OI-206

decisions.verbatim: the pedal fields stay false/-1 (suspended, OI-194)
decisions.plain: The new path does not yet mark pedal points - a sustained bass note the harmony moves over. The field is left empty rather than guessed.

decisions.title: The founding principle - analyse at the finest grain, coarser views are derived
decisions.verbatim:
**The founding principle: analyze at the finest grain where harmony is well-defined, and make everything coarser a
*derived view*.**
decisions.plain: The analysis works on the smallest stretch over which the sounding harmony does not change. Phrases, key areas and sections are then read off that, never analysed directly.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:744 heading says '(ratified; full statements in cowork_target_architecture.md)'; the date and ratifier are not stated at this home
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:748-750: analysing at the finest grain is what makes segmentation a fact rather than a judgment (over-grab becomes structurally impossible), it aligns the architecture with the per-slice oracle measurement already built, and it matches the published state of the art - Contrapunctus labels every event.

decisions.title: The atomic analysis unit is the constant-sonority slice, never the metric beat
decisions.verbatim: The atomic analysis unit is the **constant-sonority slice** (L2), never the metric beat
decisions.plain: The smallest thing analysed is a stretch during which exactly the same notes are sounding - not a beat of the bar.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:744-751. The joint estimator's own unit is the ONSET event (jointdecoder.h:67), not this slice - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-228
decisions.rationale: Same passage as D-022, ARCHITECTURE.md:746-750: the metric beat is not where harmony is well-defined; the constant-sonority slice is, and every coarser unit is derived from it.

decisions.title: The fact layers are style-agnostic; style lives only in calibration
decisions.verbatim:
L1 (notes) and L2 (slicing) are **style-agnostic and
  lossless** — they carry facts, never style. Style-specificity lives **only** in the *calibration* of the judgment
  layers (their priors/weights), **never in structure**.
decisions.plain: Reading the notes and cutting the music into constant-sound stretches works the same for every kind of music. Whether a piece is Baroque or jazz can change only the numbers the judging layers use, never the shape of the code.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:744 ratified banner; sharpens §2.1 (D-070)
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:753-756: confining style to the calibration of the judgment layers sharpens §2.1 - not merely data-driven style, but style kept out of the layers that carry facts, so the fact surface cannot silently differ between styles.

decisions.title: Forward-only, with two scoped escapes
decisions.verbatim:
The **ratified** architecture (user-ratified;
`cowork_target_architecture.md` §2) is **forward-only**:
decisions.plain: Each stage was to pass its answer forward and never reach back. A confident earlier answer could be overturned only by re-running that one stretch forwards, and the one genuinely tangled key-versus-chord case got a narrow, gated exception.
decisions.status_source: The 2026-07-17 governing decision (D-001) replaces the mechanism with ONE joint decode - the mechanism this block had ruled out. No supersession banner was added to §2.14 - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-234
decisions.rationale: Measurement, ARCHITECTURE.md:723-726: the investigation measured the full joint cross-layer search INERT, and located the realisable gain in soft-evidence quality carried forward (calibrated confidence + ranked alternatives) rather than global cycling.

decisions.title: The global joint-lattice decode was measured inert (2026-06-29)
decisions.verbatim:
The subsequent investigation
**measured the full joint cross-layer search INERT**
decisions.plain: An earlier plan to search all the possibilities at once was tested and found to add nothing, so the effort was redirected into better evidence flowing forwards.
decisions.status_source: The joint estimator (D-001) is a global joint decode and is in production on both surfaces. The record does not state how this measurement was reconciled with the later ruling - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-234
decisions.rationale: The measurement itself (ARCHITECTURE.md:723-724). What the record does NOT state is how it was reconciled with the 2026-07-17 joint estimator, which is one - see open_items/OI-234.

decisions.title: Every layer emits ranked candidates plus a confidence, never a forced point estimate
decisions.verbatim: each layer is feed-forward and emits **ranked candidates + a confidence**, never a forced point estimate;
decisions.plain: No stage is allowed to report only its single best answer. It reports the runners-up too, with a measure of how clear-cut the choice was.
decisions.status_source: The mechanism around it (D-025) is superseded in fact, but the ranked-alternatives requirement is carried forward by the joint estimator's published candidate lists (D-006)
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:681-683: irrevocable point estimates block iteration and provisional results with confidence metadata enable it, so every layer's output must carry the alternatives and the confidence a later layer would need to overturn it.

decisions.title: The span typology - every layer names the span it operates on; bare 'region' is banned
decisions.verbatim:
"Region" unqualified is **banned** as
  ambiguous; every layer names the span it operates on.
decisions.plain: The word 'region' on its own is forbidden, because it hides which kind of stretch is meant. Each stretch has its own name: the chord-span, the key-span, the punctuation-span and so on.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:765-772 records the rename CONFIRMED (user, 2026-07-02) and EXECUTED 2026-07-03 'propagated through every layer spec'. ARCHITECTURE.md itself still uses the banned word 216 times including section headings - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-233
decisions.rationale: Research citation, ARCHITECTURE.md:787 - the span typology follows the GTTM premise of independent structures (Lerdahl & Jackendoff); the ban on the bare word is because a 'region' is a FAMILY of spans and the unqualified word names none of them (:765, :786-787).

decisions.title: The verifiability contract
decisions.verbatim:
prefer what we can verify against ground truth (it is how we catch our own theory
  errors); for sound theory we cannot verify against the current corpus, build it with an explicit
  **alternative-confidence path** *and* an **"empirically-unvalidated" mark**, rather than refusing it
decisions.plain: Prefer what we can check against annotated music. Where the theory is sound but we have nothing to check it against, build it anyway - but mark it as unchecked and give it its own confidence path.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:744 ratified banner
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:794-797: checking against ground truth is how we catch our own theory errors, and refusing sound theory we cannot yet check would forfeit the jazz and pop reach, where the theory exists and the corpus does not.

decisions.title: Bounded context - cost scales with the working span, not the whole score
decisions.verbatim:
The binding scale requirements: **(R1)** cost scales with the working span, not the whole
  score; **(R2)**
  re-analysis is incremental over the dirty span plus a bounded margin; **(R3)** the working span is **extensible**
decisions.plain: Analysis runs on what the user has selected. The work must grow with the size of that selection, not with the size of the piece; re-analysis after an edit must only redo the changed part; and a layer that needs more music asks for it rather than reading everything.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:802-806 names cowork_bounded_context_design.md as the ONE detailed cross-layer spec and records the 2026-07-02 user directive making it 'the hard gate before L6'. DIRECTLY CONTRADICTED by D-011 (whole-score decode per query, no caching) - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-210/OI-212
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:798-802: the analysis runs on the user's selection, so a layer needing more must request an append-only extension from Layer 1 carrying a stop condition and a hard bound. The three binding scale requirements R1-R3 are stated there; the detailed cross-layer specification is `cowork_bounded_context_design.md`.

decisions.title: Whole-score analysis is the degenerate case, not the design
decisions.verbatim: Whole-score analysis is the degenerate case (selection = score).
decisions.plain: Analysing the whole piece is what happens when the user has selected the whole piece. It is not the normal mode of operation.
decisions.status_source: Same home as D-030. The record producer analyses the whole score regardless of the requested span (OI-212)
decisions.rationale: Same passage, ARCHITECTURE.md:802: whole-score analysis is what the bounded-context rule produces when the selection happens to be the whole score - a case of the rule, not an exception to it.

decisions.title: Every confidence crossing a layer boundary is in 0..1, class-declared, with its decision named
decisions.verbatim:
At a **layer boundary** (any value another layer may read), a confidence is **[0,1], class-declared, with
  its decision named**. Unbounded internal scores are permitted *inside* a layer but must be squashed at the boundary.
decisions.plain: Inside a stage, a confidence can be on any scale. The moment another stage can read it, it must be a 0-to-1 number, labelled with what kind of confidence it is and what decision it belongs to.
decisions.status_source: cowork_confidence_contract.md:3 'Status: RATIFIED (user, 2026-07-02)'. ARCHITECTURE.md:762 still calls it 'ratification-gated' - a stale status at the canonical home (OPEN_ITEMS OI-232, item 5). Contradicted by D-019 on the production record arm - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-231
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, `cowork_confidence_contract.md:13-21` ('Why this contract exists'): the forward-override mechanism numerically compares a later layer's contradiction strength against an earlier layer's confidence, and those quantities are incommensurable by construction today - Layer 3 publishes a sequence margin, Layer 4 a three-part composite, Layer 5 an unbounded additive score. Fitting weights cannot repair a comparison between quantities with undefined semantics; it would bury the incoherence in fitted constants.

decisions.title: Each layer owns one evidence-source-times-question contribution and uses all of L1's information
decisions.verbatim:
each layer owns one *(evidence-source × question)*
  contribution — stated as "owns the *[named evidence]* contribution to *X*", with what it does **not** own made
  explicit — defers what needs later evidence (carried as ranked alternatives + an uncertain mark), and within its scope
  uses *all* the information L1 carries losslessly (notated spelling, metric weight, voice).
decisions.plain: Each stage owns one contribution and says plainly what it does not own, handing unresolved cases forward as ranked options. Owning one contribution does not narrow what it may look at: within its scope it uses all the information the note reader carries - how the note is spelt, where it falls in the bar, and which voice it is in.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:744 ratified banner. The joint emission reads only struck notes (OI-228) and the shared tone surface is voice-blind (OI-74)
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:807-810: the single-responsibility half is what lets a layer say what it does NOT own, and the maximal-information half is what stops that ownership from being read as permission to ignore evidence Layer 1 already carries.

decisions.title: A new layer or axis is admitted only through three co-equal gates
decisions.verbatim:
**A new layer or axis is admitted only when it clears three co-equal gates,
  all required:**
decisions.plain: A new stage is added only if it carries one distinct responsibility, can be validated somehow, and buys something we can actually check. Carrying a distinct responsibility is enough on its own, even with no immediate accuracy gain.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:824-831
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:824-831: gate (1) separation of concerns is a structural mandate sufficient on its own even at zero accuracy gain; gates (2) verifiability and (3) proportionality exist against the opposite error, and the record names the reminder - Contrapunctus is competitive with the state of the art with NO explicit grouping layer.

decisions.title: The effort setting - every cost-driving choice is a setting, never a hardcoded constant
decisions.verbatim:
**(a)** every cost-driving choice is an
explicit *setting*, never a hardcoded constant; **(b)** every optional expensive refinement is a cleanly separable on/off
stage.
decisions.plain: Anything that makes the analysis slower must be something the user or the caller can turn down, not a number baked into the code; and any expensive extra step must be separable so it can be switched off.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:737-741. Not implemented: the effort setting does not exist and the decode's cost drivers (segment cap, key prune width) are compiled-in constants - tracked at OI-209/OI-210
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:737-741: the effort dial is a calibration knob, not a structural one, so its two standing rules follow - every cost-driving choice is an explicit setting, and every optional expensive refinement is a cleanly separable stage.

decisions.title: Accumulating gates are a warning sign - add iteration, not more gates
decisions.verbatim:
When a feedforward layer acquires many gates
and guards to compensate for missing upstream feedback, that is a symptom of missing
iteration — not a sign that the layer needs more gates.
decisions.plain: If a stage keeps needing new special cases, the problem is that it is missing information from elsewhere. Adding another special case makes it worse.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:657-661; restated as an ongoing concern at :2131-2136
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:657-661: each gate is a heuristic patch on a structural limitation, so a rising gate count is a symptom of missing iteration rather than an argument for more gates.

decisions.title: The note model is the single source of truth for what sounds, and reads the score once
decisions.verbatim: **The lossless, tie-resolved NOTE MODEL — the single source of truth for "what sounds."** `NoteModel::build(score)` reads the score **once**
decisions.plain: One component reads the score and works out which notes are sounding when. Everything else asks it, and nothing else reads the score.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:997-1008 (Layer 1 - Built+Live)
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1008: one read of the score into one queryable set is what makes the note model the single source of truth for what sounds; the alternative is several readers that can disagree.

decisions.title: Tied notes are one event; spans are answered by overlap with no horizon
decisions.verbatim: Tied groups are merged into **one** span/onset (via the DOM `firstTiedNote`/`lastTiedNote`/`playTicksFraction`); spans are true `[onset,release)` answered by **overlap with no horizon** (the old 4-whole-note backward cap is gone).
decisions.plain: A note tied across a barline counts once, starting where it was struck and ending where it stops. Asking what is sounding at a moment looks back as far as needed, with no arbitrary cut-off.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1008; the behaviour change it caused is the ratified trade-off at :1026-1032
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1008: tied groups are merged into one span and one onset via the score model's own tie links, and spans are answered by overlap with no horizon - which retires the old four-whole-note backward cap that could miss a longer sustain.

decisions.title: Ineligible notes are kept and flagged, never dropped
decisions.verbatim: Grace / non-playing / invisible / staff-ineligible notes are **kept and flagged, never dropped**.
decisions.plain: Notes that should not drive the analysis - grace notes, hidden notes, notes on a non-musical staff - are still recorded, marked as such. Nothing is thrown away.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1008; the standing no-information-loss principle is CLAUDE.md #12
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1008, and #12: a dropped note is information lost for good, so ineligible notes are kept and flagged and each consumer decides what to do with them.

decisions.title: The tie-unresolved atoms are republished additively for the joint estimator
decisions.verbatim: `notatedNotes()` republishes the tie-UNRESOLVED atoms — EVERY notated note incl. tie continuations, each with its OWN notated span, a `tieContinuation` flag, a `hasFermata` flag, and `resolvedIndex` linking to its tie-resolved `NoteEvent`
decisions.plain: As well as merging tied notes, the note reader also publishes them separately, each with a marker saying it is a continuation. The joint estimator needs both views.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1008 records it as 'Purely additive' under the OI-180 dual-path sanction
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1008: the tie-unresolved atoms carry the facts the tie-resolved surface discards and the joint estimator's event lattice and emission covariates need; publishing them additively keeps every existing consumer byte-identical.

decisions.title: The slicer output covers the domain with no gaps and no overlaps
decisions.verbatim: returns an ordered, **covering, lossless** list of half-open `[start,end)` spans that **tile the domain with no gaps and no overlaps**
decisions.plain: The music is cut into consecutive stretches that between them account for every moment exactly once.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1035-1045 (Layer 2 - Built+Live)
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1045: a covering, lossless tiling is what makes the slicer a fact rather than a judgment - every tick lands in exactly one slice, so nothing the score sounds can fall between slices.

decisions.title: Slice boundaries are every onset AND every release
decisions.verbatim: Boundaries = the sorted-unique union of every **onset AND every release** of the **eligible** notes; consecutive boundaries form the slices.
decisions.plain: A new stretch begins whenever any note starts and also whenever any note stops - because a note ending changes what is sounding just as much as a note beginning.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1045. Cited by open_items/OI-228 as the primary source the joint emission departs from
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1045 with :1077-1080: taking every onset AND every release makes the boundary set an exhaustive candidate grid - necessary but not sufficient - so a real chord change can never be missed and over-grab is structurally impossible.

decisions.title: Slice identity IS the eligible sounding-note set
decisions.verbatim:
**Slice identity is the eligible sounding-NOTE set** (not the octave-folded PC set — a
unison/octave shrink is a real boundary though the PC set is unchanged).
decisions.plain: What makes one stretch different from the next is the exact set of notes sounding through it - not merely which pitch names are present. Two voices collapsing onto the same note is a real change even though no pitch name was lost.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1052-1053. The joint decoder's per-event note set is ONSET-only (jointdecoder.h:67) - open_items/OI-228
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1052-1053: identity is the note set and not the octave-folded pitch-class set, because a unison or octave shrink is a real boundary even though the pitch-class set is unchanged.

decisions.title: A note that opens no boundary still rides along in the slice's sounding set
decisions.verbatim:
A muted / invisible / non-tonal-staff note opens
**no** boundary, yet still rides along in each slice's `overlapping()` set (passed through, not
dropped).
decisions.plain: A note that is not allowed to create a new stretch is still recorded as sounding during the stretches it spans.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1047-1053
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1049-1051: a slice is 'constant TONAL sonority', so an ineligible note opens no boundary; dropping it as well would lose it (#12), and it is carried as passenger metadata instead.

decisions.title: The slicer re-decides nothing about eligibility
decisions.verbatim: **Boundaries over layer-1's eligibility annotation — never re-decided.**
decisions.plain: Whether a note counts was settled by the note reader. The slicer reads that decision and does not second-guess it.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1047-1049
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1047-1049: eligibility is Layer 1's decision, and a second filter in Layer 2 would be a second place the same question is answered (#6/#7).

decisions.title: Zero interpretation - the slicer applies no thresholds and no musical judgment
decisions.verbatim:
**Zero interpretation.** No thresholds, min-gap, merge, or snapping; no notion of
"ornamental/passing/structural".
decisions.plain: The cutting-up step makes no musical decisions at all. It does not decide that a note is ornamental, does not merge short stretches, and has no adjustable numbers.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1072-1080
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1072-1074: a threshold or a merge would make the slicer a judgment; with none, its output is a fact and the judgment stays where it belongs, in the layers that decide.

decisions.title: No special-casing of any note kind
decisions.verbatim:
**No special-casing of any note kind** — grace and tuplet
outcomes fall out of the note-model spans as facts
decisions.plain: Grace notes and tuplets need no special code. Their timing is a fact the note reader already carries, and the right answer falls out of it.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1072-1077
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1073-1077, verified at the source: a grace note carries onset = the parent chord's tick and duration = its nominal written value, and tuplet ticks are the model's real un-snapped ticks, so both fall out of the note-model spans as facts and the slicer needs no grace or tuplet code at all.

decisions.title: Boundaries are necessary but not sufficient; over-grab is structurally impossible
decisions.verbatim:
Boundaries are **necessary but not sufficient** for
a chord change (the exhaustive candidate grid): a real chord change can never be missed
(over-grab is structurally impossible), and the slicer never asserts a change
decisions.plain: Every place a chord could change is offered as a candidate, so no real chord change can be missed. Whether a candidate is a real change is decided later, by a stage that judges harmony.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1077-1080
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1077-1080: because the boundary grid is exhaustive, the slicer never asserts a change - Layer 3 decides which boundaries are real and a later layer groups equal analyses.

decisions.title: An interior stretch where everything rests is an explicit empty slice, not a gap
decisions.verbatim:
An interior span where all eligible voices rest is an **explicit
EMPTY slice** (empty eligible overlap set), not a gap
decisions.plain: Silence in the middle of the music is recorded as a stretch with nothing in it, rather than as a hole in the coverage.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1055-1066
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1063-1065: an explicit empty slice falls out of the consecutive-boundary construction for free, and it keeps the covering guarantee (D-041) true through a silence, which a gap would break.

decisions.title: Slicing is clipped to the loaded span and never drags outside it
decisions.verbatim: slicing never drags outside the loaded span
decisions.plain: The slicer cuts only within the span it was handed: a note sounding across the edge of that span is cut at the edge, and the slicer never reaches outside it. Widening what is analysed is the orchestration's job, not the slicer's, and re-slicing a wider span must reproduce the narrower one exactly - which is what makes widening safe.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1055-1062; cites cowork_layer2_reslice_design.md §2
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1055-1070 with `cowork_layer2_reslice_design.md` §2: the clip is what makes re-slice equivalence hold - re-slicing an enlarged span reproduces the narrower result, with interior change-points stable and only the edge slice abutting the artificial boundary extending - so extending the span is lawful rather than a re-analysis.

decisions.title: The production key/mode path is the sequence decoder, not the per-stretch resolver
decisions.verbatim: **The production region key/mode path is the decoder, not the per-region resolver.**
decisions.plain: The tonality is worked out for the whole piece at once, as a sequence, rather than separately for each stretch.
decisions.status_source: The joint estimator now decides key on both surfaces (D-005, D-010). The Layer-3 section still reads 'Built+Live' - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-232

decisions.title: The signature read and declared-mode mapping live in ONE shared function
decisions.verbatim:
The signature read + declared-mode
mapping + declared-gated Baroque `partialSignatureCorrection` was lifted verbatim into a shared
public `resolveKeySignatureContext`, **called by both** the resolver and the wiring — so no
signature/partial-correction logic is duplicated.
decisions.plain: Reading the printed key signature and turning it into a starting assumption happens in one place that both callers use, so the two cannot drift apart.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1114-1119

decisions.title: The tick-local path keeps the older resolver (the ratified P4-defer)
decisions.verbatim:
**P4 tick-local still uses `resolveKeyAndModeRanked` + `collectPitchContext`** (the ratified
  P4-defer).
decisions.plain: One narrow fallback - answering about a single moment when no surrounding stretch is available - still uses the older method. That was a deliberate deferral.
decisions.status_source: On the switched build the note-seam funnel returns from the record arm before this fallback is reachable (notationcomposingbridge.cpp:728-738). The D-P4 revisit trigger (D-063) was never discharged

decisions.title: All 21 modes are scored against all 12 tonics; the harmonic major family is deferred
decisions.verbatim:
Harmonic major modes are
significantly rarer as tonal centers than melodic and harmonic minor modes, and the
validation corpus is unlikely to calibrate them well.
decisions.plain: The key finder considers 21 scale types on each of the 12 possible tonics. The harmonic major family was left out because it is rare and we have no annotated music to calibrate it against.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:2148-2149 (21 modes), :2213-2217 (harmonic major deferred)
decisions.rationale: Recorded for the DEFERRAL half only, ARCHITECTURE.md:2213-2217: the harmonic major modes are significantly rarer as tonal centers than the melodic and harmonic minor modes, and the validation corpus is unlikely to calibrate them well. Why the other 21 modes are all scored against all 12 tonics has no recorded derivation.

decisions.title: The 21 mode priors are independent and user-configurable
decisions.verbatim:
**21 independent additive priors**, one per mode, user-configurable
  via `IComposingAnalysisConfiguration::modePrior{ModeName}()`
decisions.plain: How likely each scale type is considered to be is a separate adjustable number per scale type, exposed in the preferences.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:2162-2164, :3020-3073. Superseded on the production path by D-003 (inference is preset-independent)

decisions.title: Notes always win - the notated key signature is a weak hint, not a bypass
decisions.verbatim:
The key/mode inferrer always runs. The notated key signature's `KeyMode` enum
(`MAJOR`, `MINOR`, etc.) is no longer a bypass gate — it is passed as a weak hint
(`declaredMode`) to `analyzeKeyMode()`
decisions.plain: The key printed at the start of the score does not settle the question. It only nudges the answer; what the notes actually do decides.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:3118-3130
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:3120-3122: the notated signature is what the composer wrote down, not what the music does - a piece may modulate, be notated in a partial signature, or contradict its own signature - so it enters as a weak hint the sounding notes can outvote.

decisions.title: The priority of evidence - actual sounding notes are the strongest evidence
decisions.verbatim: | Strongest | Actual sounding notes | what is literally happening now |
decisions.plain: In deciding the key, what is actually sounding right now outranks the surrounding bars, which outrank the printed key signature, which outranks the major/minor tag on it.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:3134-3141. Cited by open_items/OI-228 as the primary source the joint emission departs from. NOT catchable by the harvest's signature net - the reason this adjudication had to read the specifications in full
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:3134-3141: the priority table ranks the actual sounding notes the strongest evidence, above the notated signature and above any prior result, for the same reason as D-056.

decisions.title: The piece-start shortcut
decisions.verbatim:
when the
analysis tick is within the first 16 quarter-note beats (a separate constant from the 16-beat lookback window below —
they coincide in value, not by design), no prior result exists (`prevResult == nullptr`),
and the key signature carries an explicit mode, the function returns the declared mode
immediately (confidence 0.5) rather than waiting for pitch evidence that cannot yet exist.
decisions.plain: At the very start of a piece there is not yet enough music to judge the key, so if the score declares major or minor the program simply believes it, marked as a middling-confidence answer.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:3125-3130 calls it 'a deliberate pragmatic choice for the score opening, not a general bypass'. NOT catchable by the harvest's signature net

decisions.title: The temporal window - 16 beats back, 8 beats forward, decayed
decisions.verbatim: The bridge uses a 16-beat lookback + 8-beat lookahead window:
decisions.plain: To judge the key at a point, the program looks about four bars back and two bars forward, giving less weight to music further away.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:3161-3173; legacy-arm only since the switch (D-010). Derivation not recorded: the only stated basis for 16 and 8 is the in-code gloss '~4 measures in 4/4' / '~2 measures ahead' (ARCHITECTURE.md:3166-3167) - no theory citation and no measurement

decisions.title: The legacy chord analyzer is a vertical sonority analyzer - keep the boundary clean
decisions.verbatim:
Do not
attempt to improve corpus agreement by adding heuristics to `RuleBasedChordAnalyzer`
that embed contextual assumptions — keep the vertical/contextual boundary clean.
decisions.plain: The chord identifier is meant to say what chord the notes sounding at one moment spell, and nothing more. Improving its score by teaching it about what came before or after was explicitly forbidden.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1853-1879. Contradicted by the same document's §4.1b/§4.1d contextual bonuses, which score a candidate from the neighbouring chords - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-235
decisions.rationale: Measurement, ARCHITECTURE.md:1859-1879: the boundary is recorded as empirically validated against DCML annotations over four corpora (2026-04-06), and the residual disagreement is diagnosed rather than assumed - 95.8 % of the bass-is-root disagreements are three-note triads in inversion, which local note content cannot resolve. Improving past that ceiling is stated to need a contextual harmony layer, NOT heuristics inside the vertical analyzer. (The same section then specifies contextual bonuses - open_items/OI-235.)

decisions.title: Gate thresholds are Baroque-calibrated and must not be loosened for other styles
decisions.verbatim:
They must not be
loosened to accommodate other styles. When a gate causes regressions in a non-Baroque
preset, the fix is either (a) a tighter structural entry condition that excludes the
problematic chord type in all styles, or (b) a preset-specific threshold value
decisions.plain: The adjustable cut-offs in the chord scorer were tuned on Baroque music. If they misbehave on other music, tighten the entry condition for everyone or give that style its own value - never widen the Baroque one.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1573-1581; the same policy is in CLAUDE.md 'Gate threshold and preset policy'
decisions.rationale: Measurement, ARCHITECTURE.md:1573-1581 and `CLAUDE.md` gate policy: the values are empirically calibrated against the Baroque corpus and are Baroque-specific, so loosening one to accommodate another style silently re-tunes the style they were measured on; the two sanctioned fixes are a tighter structural entry condition that excludes the chord type in all styles, or a preset-specific override leaving the Baroque default unchanged.

decisions.title: Progression signals are withheld while segmentation is being explored
decisions.verbatim:
the progression signals are withheld
during `greedyExpandSegmentation`'s internal boundary-exploration calls, which run in
`ScoringPhase::Segmentation` — prevents the bonus from biasing segmentation
before the final per-region pass
decisions.plain: While the program is still deciding where one chord ends and the next begins, the bonuses that reward a chord for fitting its neighbours are switched off, so that the answer does not bias the question.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1776-1779, :1816-1822; the residual coupling is recorded as debt at :2105-2112
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1776-1779 (the withheld signals 'prevent the bonus from biasing segmentation before the final per-region pass') with :641-644: where a boundary falls decides which pitch classes land in each candidate's input, and chord identity is itself a signal for where boundaries should be - so letting progression signals score the exploratory passes would let the answer decide its own input.

decisions.title: Cold context on the tick-local path is the accepted contract
decisions.verbatim:
Cold context on P4 is the **current contract**, documented and accepted (the same
precedent as the Stage 2.3 diagnose context banner: a path may legitimately analyze with less
context, provided that is stated, not silent).
decisions.plain: One narrow path analyses a moment without knowing what came before. That is allowed because it is written down, not hidden.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1284-1301. Its revisit trigger - 'Stage 3 design must state explicitly what P4 (and the bridge) consume from the decode' (:1299-1300) - has not been discharged by the joint/record design

decisions.title: The chord-scoring presets are a measurement-only artifact
decisions.verbatim:
The
chord-scoring preset system is currently a **measurement-only artifact** of `batch_analyze`. Do
**not** silently flip the live product onto preset chordPrefs
decisions.plain: The Baroque and Jazz chord-scoring settings exist only in the measurement tool. The program the user runs has never used them, and switching it over would be a product decision, not a code tidy-up.
decisions.status_source: D-003 makes inference preset-independent on the production path, so the divergence this decision manages no longer exists there; it still describes the legacy path

decisions.title: The look-ahead divergence between the two paths is intentional and load-bearing
decisions.verbatim: **D1 — `excludeLookAheadOnDenseStart`** is **intentionally divergent and load-bearing.**
decisions.plain: One setting deliberately differs between the measurement tool and the program, because making them the same made the program worse on a specific repertoire.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1263-1266, restated at :1363-1366

decisions.title: Chord symbols written in the score are never analyzer input
decisions.verbatim:
chord symbols must never be used as analyzer input in
production because they are user content and may be incorrect.
decisions.plain: The chord names already written in a score are the user's own text and may be wrong. The analysis reads only the notes, the key signature and the settings.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:2300-2302, restated as the retirement rationale's 'Core principle' at :2335-2337
patterns: never be used as analyzer input
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:2300-2302: written chord symbols are USER CONTENT and may be incorrect, so reading them back as input would make the analyzer agree with whatever it was given rather than with the notes. The `--inject-written-root` flag is kept as a diagnostic upper bound and is explicitly not a production path.

decisions.title: Jazz mode (chord-symbol-driven boundaries) is retired
decisions.verbatim: **Status: Retired** — production analysis paths in commit 02e3733afb, tool-side surfaces in 69716deead. Chord symbols are no longer read by any analysis or tool path.
decisions.plain: The separate jazz analysis mode that took its stretch boundaries from written chord symbols has been removed entirely.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:2269, retirement rationale at :2324-2339

decisions.title: The chord identifier needs at least three distinct pitch classes
decisions.verbatim: Minimum 3 distinct pitch classes required. Returns empty vector if insufficient data.
decisions.plain: With fewer than three different pitch names sounding, the chord identifier declines to answer rather than guessing.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1605

decisions.title: Two identity modes for merged stretches - harmonic summary and as-written
decisions.verbatim:
**Harmonic summary mode** (status bar, analysis, tuning): region identity = root pitch
class + quality.
decisions.plain: When neighbouring stretches are merged, they count as the same chord if the root and the major/minor character match. A second mode that would also require the exact voicing to match is designed but not built.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1722 'Region identity modes (decided 2026-04-11)'; :1734-1736 records as-written mode deferred

decisions.title: Style behaviour is fully data-driven - no conditional logic on style identity
decisions.verbatim:
The C++ implementation contains no conditional logic based on style identity. All
behavioral differences between musical styles are expressed as parameter values in
style JSON files.
decisions.plain: Nowhere does the code ask 'is this jazz?'. Differences between styles are numbers in a settings file.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:381-384 states the §2 principles are 'hard constraints, not guidelines'; restated at §2.4 :435-438
patterns: no conditional logic based on style
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:388-390 with the worked wrong/correct pair at :392-402: if behaviour branched on a style's identity, adding or renaming a style would require C++ changes; driving it from parameters means it never does.

decisions.title: The analysis layer never produces display strings
decisions.verbatim:
Analysis components produce structured data — they never produce display strings.
Formatting is handled by separate formatter classes.
decisions.plain: The analysis returns facts. Turning those facts into text on screen is somebody else's job.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:429-433; mechanically guarded for the joint module by D-017
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:431-433: the separation is already established by `ChordSymbolFormatter`, and keeping it means the same analysis can be rendered several ways without the analysis knowing about any of them.

decisions.title: The dependency rule - the analysis library knows nothing about the score format
decisions.verbatim: This dependency order is **enforced**. Any code that would invert it (e.g. a composing header forward-declaring `mu::engraving::Note`) must be moved to the notation bridge layer.
decisions.plain: The music-theory library must not know how MuseScore stores a score. Anything that needs both lives in a thin bridge layer in between.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:941-972, checklist at :1424-1431

decisions.title: Single implementation for shared logic; mirroring is a last resort
decisions.verbatim:
Any algorithm that must produce identical results in both the notation bridge and
`batch_analyze` belongs in the `composing` module (`src/composing/`), not in either
consumer.
decisions.plain: If the program and the measurement tool must agree, the code that makes them agree lives in one shared place. Copying it into both is a last resort that must be flagged as debt.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:482-515; the standing project-wide form is CLAUDE.md #6 (total unification)
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:484-502: the notation bridge and `batch_analyze` must produce identical results, so shared logic lives in the composing module both call; mirroring is permitted only when a shared implementation is blocked by a dependency constraint, and then only with a marked technical-debt note.

decisions.title: Analyze and suggest - never modify the score without explicit user action
decisions.verbatim:
The system presents analytical findings and suggestions. It never modifies the main score
automatically. All score modifications require explicit user action.
decisions.plain: The program tells you what it thinks. It never changes your music unless you ask it to.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:473-480
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:475-480: the chord staff, the status bar and the panels are informational - they show what was inferred - and every change to the music is the user's explicit act through standard MuseScore editing.

decisions.title: Interface-based design for machine-learning substitutability
decisions.verbatim:
Every component that may eventually be replaced or augmented by a machine learning
model must be defined behind a pure abstract interface.
decisions.plain: Anything that might one day be replaced by a trained model is hidden behind an interface, so the replacement can be dropped in without touching everything else.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:404-427; the substitution points are listed at §14.1
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:406-408: the rest of the system depends only on the interface, so a machine-learning implementation can replace a rule-based one without any consumer changing.

decisions.title: Score inspection before diagnosis
decisions.verbatim:
Claude Code does not have direct score access and must not substitute
statistical inference for visual score inspection.
decisions.plain: When a corpus number looks odd, somebody opens the actual music and looks at it before anyone changes code or runs more statistics.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:517-545
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:524-545: score inspection takes two minutes and answers what corpus statistics cannot - the actual texture, whether the chord staff is over-segmenting, whether the opening key is right - and Claude Code has no score access, so it must not substitute statistical inference for looking.

decisions.title: The configuration interface is split into two narrow IoC interfaces
decisions.verbatim: The implode bridge has no business knowing about status-bar display preferences; the analysis bridge has no business knowing about chord-staff output settings.
decisions.plain: Settings are exposed through two small interfaces rather than one big one, so each component can only see the settings it actually needs.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1394-1406, restated at :2967-2978

decisions.title: The cross-layer value types live in a dependency-free leaf header
decisions.verbatim: **The cross-layer value-types LEAF** — a dependency-free header (STL only; no `chord/`, `key/`, or engraving includes) holding the value types that cross the L1.5 / L3 / L4 boundaries
decisions.plain: The small data types that several stages share live in one header that depends on nothing, which removed two places where a lower stage had to include a higher one.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1238-1246

decisions.title: The function layer annotates and resolves; it never rewrites the committed chord
decisions.verbatim:
additive over L4 (it annotates and resolves; it never
rewrites the committed chord identity)
decisions.plain: The stage that works out a chord's role in the key may label it and settle open questions, but it may not change which chord was identified.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1192-1201 (Layer 5 - Built+Dormant, design ratified)

decisions.title: Carried abstentions are resolved by selecting among the carried readings, never re-derived
decisions.verbatim: the carried L4 abstentions are resolved by **selecting** among the carried readings (never re-derived)
decisions.plain: Where the chord stage could not decide, the function stage picks from the options it was handed. It does not work the chord out again from the notes.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1192-1201

decisions.title: The cadence detector is key-agnostic
decisions.verbatim:
The cadence
detector is **key-agnostic** (it votes for the key; it does not read a resolved key).
decisions.plain: The part that spots cadences must not be told what key it is in - it is one of the things that decides the key, so reading the answer first would be circular.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1200. open_items/OI-166 records that the built detector is key-agnostic but CHORD-derived, not the bass-driven pre-scan specified

decisions.title: The grouping layer is additive, read-only, with no feedback
decisions.verbatim: additive, read-only, no feedback into L5.
decisions.plain: The stage that assembles phrases and key areas only organises what earlier stages decided. It never changes their answers.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1203-1210 (Layer 6 - Design-only, v1 spec)

decisions.title: Hierarchy, periods and prolongation are out of the validatable core
decisions.verbatim:
Hierarchy,
periods/sentences, and prolongation are out of the validatable core (verifiability contract, §2.15).
decisions.plain: Deeper structural theory - nested hierarchy, periods, prolongation - is deliberately left out, because we have no annotated music to check it against.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1203-1210, deriving from D-029

decisions.title: The progression-schema recognizer is a consumer of the function layer, not a new layer
decisions.verbatim: an L5 *consumer* (a prior + an annotation), not a new layer
decisions.plain: Recognising well-known chord patterns is something that reads the finished analysis and annotates it. It is not another stage in the chain.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1212-1217 'Scaffolding-first, deferred'

decisions.title: The voice-leading axis is a separate axis with its own layers
decisions.verbatim:
the **orthogonal voice-leading axis** with its own layers (where melodic phrases [MT] and
  chord **voicing / arrangement** are analysed)
decisions.plain: How the individual voices move is a second, independent line of analysis alongside the harmonic one, with its own stages.

decisions.title: Roman numerals and Nashville numbers are presentation choices, not separate analyses
decisions.verbatim:
Roman numerals and Nashville numbers are **presentation choices**, not
  separate analyses — they are alternative formatters on the same `ChordAnalysisResult`.
decisions.plain: Showing the harmony as Roman numerals or as Nashville numbers is a choice of how to display one and the same analysis.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:2991-2995; consistent with D-016
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:5505-5507: Roman numerals and Nashville numbers encode identical information, so showing both on one staff would be redundant and would destroy legibility - which makes the choice a display preference, not two analyses.

decisions.title: Display options live with the formatter, not with the analyzer preferences
decisions.verbatim:
Display options (`Options`) live in `ChordSymbolFormatter`, not in
`ChordAnalyzerPreferences`, enforcing the analysis/display separation (principle 2.3).
decisions.plain: Which spelling convention to use on screen is a formatter setting, kept away from the settings that affect the analysis itself.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:2672-2707

decisions.title: No automatic key signature injection
decisions.verbatim:
No automatic key signature
injection is planned.
decisions.plain: The program will never add a key signature to your score by itself. It shows what it inferred in the chord staff and leaves the decision to you.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:3588-3596; an instance of D-074

decisions.title: The legacy confidence exposure gates - 0.5 tentative, 0.8 assertive
decisions.verbatim:
- Above 0.8 — display without qualifier
- 0.5–0.8 — append "?" to key/mode label
- Below 0.5 — suppress key-dependent chord-track annotations rather than exposing a low-confidence key
decisions.plain: On the old path, a key the program is unsure of is shown with a question mark, and one it is very unsure of is not shown at all rather than shown wrongly.

decisions.title: Abstention is a valid outcome - high precision before coverage
decisions.verbatim:
- high precision on exposed results
- calibrated abstention when evidence is weak
decisions.plain: The aim is not to put a label on everything. It is to be right about what we do label, and to say nothing when the evidence is thin.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:3287-3339
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:3294-3302 and its consumer rules at :5604-5612: the stated product target is not 'always emit a label' but high precision on exposed results, calibrated abstention when evidence is weak, and coverage gains only after precision is acceptable - so below the confidence bar the key-dependent annotations are suppressed rather than printed tentatively.

decisions.title: ARCHITECTURE.md is the canonical architecture document and wins every disagreement
decisions.verbatim:
**When any doc disagrees with
> this one, this one wins, and a new ratified decision lands here first.**
decisions.plain: Where two documents disagree about the architecture, this one is right, and a new ruling must be written into it before anywhere else.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:256-264 'Doc governance (2026-06-29) - the hierarchy'
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:256-264: the per-layer design documents are the authoritative detail for their own scope but are not rival architecture documents; without one document that wins, a reader has no way to resolve a disagreement between two.

decisions.title: A cross-cutting contract is stated once and never redefined in a layer document
decisions.verbatim:
a **cross-cutting contract is stated once, here (§2.15), and never redefined in a
> layer doc**
decisions.plain: Rules that apply to every stage are written down in one place. A stage's own document may use such a rule but may not restate it in its own words.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:256-264
decisions.rationale: Same passage, ARCHITECTURE.md:260-261: a cross-cutting contract restated in a layer document is a second copy that can drift (#6); a layer document may USE the span typology or the verifiability contract, not redefine them.

decisions.title: STATUS.md wins on current state; ARCHITECTURE.md on design
decisions.verbatim:
Where a
> heading's status and STATUS.md disagree, STATUS.md wins. This section describes the **designs**.
decisions.plain: For what is built right now, read STATUS.md. For what was decided, read this document. Where they disagree about built-or-not, STATUS.md is right.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:3101-3103, consistent with :251-254
patterns: Update STATUS\.md as your last act
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:251-254 and :3102-3103: the two documents move on different clocks - current state changes every session, design changes only when a decision changes - so each owns the question it can keep current.

decisions.title: Each layer carries exactly one build state
decisions.verbatim:
Each layer below is tagged with exactly one build state: **Built+Live** (wired into the
production pipeline), **Built+Dormant** (built and tested but not wired — reachable only via diagnostics, byte-identical on
production), or **Design-only** (specified, not yet built).
decisions.plain: Every stage is labelled as live, built-but-not-connected, or designed-only - one label each, no ambiguity.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:986-989. Three layer tags and two prose statements are stale after the switch - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-232

decisions.title: The dual path during the joint-estimator build is a declared, bounded, pre-ratified migration state
decisions.verbatim: STAGED SCOPE (declared migration state, #23)
decisions.plain: Building the new estimator beside the old one temporarily breaks the rule that there is one way to do each thing. That was declared in advance, bounded, and given a retirement plan.
decisions.status_source: open_items/OI-180 (PROTOCOL RATIFIED 2026-07-19; forward exit EXECUTED on both surfaces 2026-07-27). The ARCHITECTURE.md text at :39-40 still says the notation layer stays legacy - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-232
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, `CLAUDE.md` principle #23 and open_items/OI-180: an end-state principle (#6, one path per concern) that a planned change must temporarily violate needs a lawful transition - the violation declared, bounded, and pre-ratified with a retirement map - so that migration is a first-class state rather than an undeclared exception.

decisions.title: Fitted values are fit once against ground truth, never per-case tuned
decisions.verbatim: forms from theory, values fit ONCE against GT (#19), never per-case tuned
decisions.plain: The shape of each piece of evidence comes from music theory. Its numerical strength is learned once from annotated music, and never adjusted to make a particular passage come out right.
decisions.status_source: OPEN_ITEMS.md:15-26 (the governing architecture decision banner). NOT recorded in any ARCHITECTURE.md layer specification - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-237
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, OPEN_ITEMS.md:25 (the governing architecture decision banner) with `CLAUDE.md` #8 and DEFECT_TYPES.md DT-2: a value tuned per case is fitted to the case and measures nothing on the next one.

decisions.title: Held-out evaluation and a capacity budget are declared before any fit
decisions.verbatim: 5-fold CV grouped by WiR file, all fitted objects train-fold-only, headline = pooled CV + piece-bootstrap CI
decisions.plain: Before the estimator's numbers are learned, we say in advance which music will be held back to test them on, and how many numbers we are allowed to learn at all. The headline number is always the one measured on the held-back music.
decisions.status_source: open_items/OI-176 and OI-177 (PROTOCOL RATIFIED 2026-07-19). The standing principles are CLAUDE.md #20. NOT recorded in any ARCHITECTURE.md layer specification - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-237
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, `CLAUDE.md` #20: no value is graded on data that helped fit it, so the split and the capacity budget are declared BEFORE fitting and the headline claim is the held-out figure; a fitted-and-self-measured number is not established (#19). The ratified protocols are open_items/OI-176 (5-fold cross-validation grouped by ground-truth file) and OI-177 (parameter inventory, cell own-estimate only at count >= 20, <= 12 weights).

decisions.title: The exact-decode reserve - the declared prune was never adopted
decisions.verbatim: the exact-decode reserve is the declared remedy (never budgeted at fitted weights)
decisions.plain: The estimator was meant to be allowed to narrow its search when that gets too slow. The narrowing rule that was specified turned out to cost more than it saved, so the estimator still searches exactly - and how it actually narrows in practice was never specified.
decisions.status_source: open_items/OI-188 (OPEN - 'bounds every ceiling claim'); the admission rule actually in production has no ratified basis (open_items/OI-226)
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, `cowork_joint_estimator_factorization.md:170-173`: exact decode is expected tractable at chorale-scale event counts, and the reserve prune is an inference technique requiring its own established-loss measurement, never a silent heuristic. What the decoder actually prunes has no recorded derivation at all (open_items/OI-226).

decisions.title: Negative evidence is information - a ruled-out possibility is carried, not dropped
decisions.verbatim:
Negative/exclusion evidence is information ("finding by exclusion") —
   carry a ruled-out possibility at low confidence rather than dropping it, unless the exclusion is
   recomputable from what is kept.
decisions.plain: Knowing that something is not the case is itself useful. A reading that has been ruled out is kept at low confidence rather than thrown away, unless we could work out the exclusion again from what we did keep.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md guiding principle #12, ratified 2026-07-06. NOT recorded in any ARCHITECTURE.md layer specification, though it governs every layer's output surface - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-237
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, `CLAUDE.md` #12: a ruled-out possibility is evidence - finding by exclusion - so it is carried at low confidence unless the exclusion is recomputable from what is kept.

decisions.title: Every derived fact is published exactly once, on the producing layer's output surface
decisions.verbatim:
every derived analytical fact is **published exactly once, on the producing layer's output surface;
consumers read, never re-derive.**
decisions.plain: Whatever a stage works out, it publishes on its own output surface; every later stage reads that instead of working it out again. Facts that are hints a later stage might one day use are published broadly even when nothing reads them yet, each carrying whether it has been established, because a consumer may not rely on an unestablished fact. What to do with a fact nobody reads is decided case by case: keep it with a named future reader stated, or remove it - and a reader outside the analysis counts.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md 'Fact-publication corollary to #6/#7/#12', ratified 2026-07-10, amended 2026-07-12 (publish EVIDENCE-class facts broadly, each carrying its establishment status). NOT recorded in any ARCHITECTURE.md layer specification - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-237
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, `CLAUDE.md` fact-publication corollary, with its evidence named there: `cowork_siloed_facts_audit.md` found 17 instances of facts being re-derived rather than read. The 2026-07-12 amendment's own recorded reason is the user's: a visible spread of published evidence lets a future design RECOGNIZE facts it would never have thought to ask for.

decisions.title: Contextual inversion bonuses fire only for major and minor candidates
decisions.verbatim:
Bonuses never fire for
Diminished, HalfDiminished, Augmented, or Suspended candidates — only Major and Minor.
decisions.plain: The bonuses that let a neighbouring chord tip an inversion reading were restricted to plain major and minor chords, after three earlier attempts without that restriction all made things worse.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1931-1939 records Iter 46 extending the same helpers to Augmented and HalfDiminished. The §4.1b statement carries no supersession note - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-236
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1643-1646: recorded as a hard-won safety constraint, the lesson of a three-attempt history in which the bonuses fired on qualities they were not measured on.

decisions.title: Augmented and half-diminished candidates receive the inversion bonuses too (Iter 46)
decisions.verbatim:
Extending these gates put Augmented and
HalfDiminished inversion candidates on equal footing with Major/Minor.
decisions.plain: The restriction above was later relaxed for augmented and half-diminished chords, because without the bonuses their correct inverted readings never reached the shortlist at all. It was the single largest improvement of that iteration path.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1929-1942 (Iter 46, commit 36bf4738a8)
decisions.rationale: Measurement, ARCHITECTURE.md:1931-1939: keeping D-101's constraint made correct inverted readings unreachable, and extending the two helper predicates to augmented and half-diminished was 'the largest single improvement of iteration path 1'.

decisions.title: Pedal-point detection is a second pass, accepted only on two conditions
decisions.verbatim:
**Pass 2** is triggered only when the Pass 1 bass PC is NOT a chord tone of the
winner.
decisions.plain: When the lowest note does not belong to the chord the upper voices spell, the program re-analyses without it. It accepts that reading only if the upper voices give at least two different pitch names and the answer is clearly better than the next different-rooted one.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:3613-3643 'Status: Implemented (Session 18, master fb9a27ce9a)'. Suspended on the record arm - see D-021
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:3617-3622: a single pass over an organ point either forces a bass-root reading and suppresses the upper-voice harmony, or returns a slash chord with the wrong root when a template accidentally fits. The 'different-root competitor' detail carries its own recorded reason at :3640-3643 - several templates share a root, so a gap measured against rank 2 collapses to about 0.047 and blocks detection for bare triads.

decisions.title: The bass-is-root bonus is conditioned on corroborating support
decisions.verbatim:
`bassNoteRootBonus` is now conditioned on corroborating root-position support in the
accumulated tones:
decisions.plain: Being the lowest note no longer counts as strong evidence of being the chord's root unless the chord above actually supports that reading. Without a third or fifth above it, the bonus almost vanishes.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:3400-3448; the failure it fixed is documented across four corpora at :3406-3419
decisions.rationale: Measurement, ARCHITECTURE.md:3405-3424: four corpora (Chopin mazurka, Mozart sonata, Corelli trio sonata, Beethoven quartet) were inspected at the score and found to share ONE mechanism - the bass moves faster than the harmonic rhythm, so each bass note independently takes the bonus and overrides the root the chord tones above already identify. The fix conditions the bonus on corroborating root-position support rather than shrinking it.

decisions.title: The spelling written in the score is read through ONE shared interpreter
decisions.verbatim:
read through the **shared** `engravingbridge::lineOfFifths` primitive (the Layer-1.5 spelling
  view) — one interpreter, not a per-layer tpc copy.
decisions.plain: How a note is spelt on the page - F sharp versus G flat - is interpreted in one shared place, not re-implemented by each stage that needs it.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1171-1174. ARCHITECTURE.md:1182-1186 records the unification residual: the legacy scorer still carries its own second reader until the legacy path retires
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1172-1174 - 'one interpreter, not a per-layer tpc copy' (#6): two interpreters of the notated spelling can disagree, and open_items/OI-173 records what that costs when it happens (four inequivalent definitions of the same predicate).

decisions.title: The augmented-sixth labels are gated to the Standard and Baroque presets
decisions.verbatim:
Gated to
Standard and Baroque presets only. Jazz and Nashville presets continue to
emit chromatic Roman numerals or chord symbols respectively.
decisions.plain: The specific Italian, French and German augmented-sixth labels are shown only under the classical presets.
decisions.status_source: open_items/OI-112 already records this preset-gating as stale; open_items/OI-201 records that the record arm collapses the family to a plain major triad symbol

decisions.title: American English throughout
decisions.verbatim: All identifiers, comments, and documentation use American English spelling.
decisions.plain: Analyzer, not analyser; color, not colour.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:440-450; restated in CLAUDE.md Conventions
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:440-450: MuseScore's own codebase is American English, so one spelling convention throughout is what keeps identifiers matching across the boundary.

decisions.title: Cross-platform by default
decisions.verbatim:
All code must run on every platform officially supported by MuseScore Studio: Windows,
macOS, and Linux.
decisions.plain: Everything must work on Windows, macOS and Linux; platform-specific code is allowed only where unavoidable and must be walled off.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:624-630
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:624-630: the code must run on every platform MuseScore Studio officially supports, so platform-specific code is permitted only when unavoidable and must be abstracted so the rest of the module stays platform-agnostic.

decisions.title: The open-items register is the one home for every unresolved issue, and the index is the status of record
decisions.verbatim:
this file is the complete INDEX and
> the **authoritative status surface**
decisions.plain: Every known unresolved problem has exactly one row in one file, and that row - not the longer write-up beside it - is the official statement of where it stands.
decisions.status_source: OPEN_ITEMS.md:3-13; the standing rule is in CLAUDE.md 'The open-items register'
patterns: index row AND its detail file
decisions.rationale: Measurement, OPEN_ITEMS.md:3-5: the register was created after a full-repository sweep found 91 open items scattered across 12 tracking surfaces with 11 status contradictions.

decisions.title: The decisions register records what was decided and its status - nothing else
decisions.verbatim:
**The register holds WHAT WAS DECIDED, and its status. Nothing else.** The proposed
   `conformance` field is REMOVED.
decisions.plain: This decisions register says what was decided and whether it still stands. Whether the code obeys it is tracked separately, in the open-items register, because those two things change on different clocks.
decisions.status_source: open_items/OI-208.md:46-67 (SHAPE RATIFIED, three rulings)
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, open_items/OI-208.md:49-54 (the user's recorded rationale): a decision's status changes only when someone rules again, whereas whether the code obeys it changes every time the code moves. Holding both in one row produces a register that silently goes stale - the exact failure the issue register was created to end.

decisions.title: A decision belongs in the owning layer's specification; the register is an index
decisions.verbatim:
**A decision belongs, wherever possible, in the OWNING LAYER'S SPECIFICATION** — that layer's
   section of `ARCHITECTURE.md` — and the register is the **index and pointer**, never a
   substitute home.
decisions.plain: A decision about how a stage should work is written into that stage's part of the architecture document. This decisions register only points at it.
decisions.status_source: open_items/OI-208.md:46-67; follows the CLAUDE.md Conventions rule of 2026-07-28
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, open_items/OI-208.md:55-62: the layer specification is where a reader looks for how a layer should work, so a register that held the decision instead of pointing at it would become a second home (#6) and the specification would stay silent.

decisions.title: Never work from memory instead of documented facts
decisions.verbatim:
No assertion, design, decision, dispatch or report may rest on recalled or
  inferred content when a documented source exists. Open the primary source and cite it
  (file:line).
decisions.plain: If a document records something, read it and quote it rather than remembering it. Being right from memory does not count, because correct memory and incorrect memory look the same until you check.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md Conventions, user-directed 2026-07-28; its founding instance is the Layer-2 note-collection reading that this adjudication's method is built to prevent
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, `CLAUDE.md` Conventions, with its founding instance recorded there: correct memory is indistinguishable from incorrect memory without checking, and the check is what surfaces the parts the memory did not contain - on 2026-07-28 the Layer-2 specification turned out to state explicitly and twice what had been reported as ambiguous.

decisions.title: Music-theory words are reserved for their music-theory meaning
decisions.verbatim:
Any term that coincides even slightly with music theory is used
  ONLY in its musical sense.
decisions.plain: In this project a score is a piece of music, a key is a tonality, and a measure is a bar. Where a word is needed in its everyday computing sense, it must be qualified - candidate score, map key, measurement.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md Conventions, user-directed 2026-07-28; open_items/OI-229 records the convention STANDING for new writing and the tree-wide cleanup as an unratified future work item
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, `CLAUDE.md` Conventions, user-directed 2026-07-28: this is a music-analysis system, so an ambiguous domain vocabulary makes every document harder to read and every specification easier to misapply.

decisions.title: The decoder commits its best path; there is no abstention on the key axis
decisions.verbatim: **key-abstain 0** — A commits its MAP path, the OI-33 flag reads zero
decisions.plain: The joint estimator always names a key. It never declines to answer on the key axis, so the abstention counter is always zero.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md gate block (A), the OI-178 adoption baselines. NOT recorded in any ARCHITECTURE.md layer specification, and it sits in tension with D-090 (calibrated abstention) - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-237

decisions.title: The regression stop is the granularity-robust unit; root governs, key and Roman numeral ride beside
decisions.verbatim:
the **class-(b) (pitch-class-decidable-root) root-disagree DURATION
  must be NON-INCREASING** vs the committed reference — the *meaningful* functional errors never grow.
decisions.plain: A change is allowed to ship only if the total amount of music on which we name the wrong chord root - counted where the root is decidable at all - does not grow. The key and the Roman numeral are watched alongside but do not govern.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md gate block (A), ratified R10-b 2026-07-06; supersedes the batch case-identity stop preserved as block (C)
decisions.rationale: Measurement, `CLAUDE.md` gate block (C): the batch region gate it replaced under-counted the true per-onset root error by roughly 15 to 56 times - it measured a small music21-filtered corner in which pitch-class-undecidable rotations were about 53 % of the residual, against about 3.5 % on the robust unit - so the robust unit is governed by the meaningful errors and is segmentation-invariant by construction.
